dublinCore.description: Interactive comparison of amplitude modulation (AM) and frequency modulation (FM) of a sinusoidal carrier by a sinusoidal message. Sliders set the carrier amplitude Ac, message amplitude Am, carrier frequency fc and message frequency fm; the sim shows the modulated waveform with its envelope or message, read-outs of the modulation index, peak deviation and bandwidth, and the amplitude spectrum with the carrier and sideband lines.
relation: Chapter 2: Introduction to Signals and Systems

searchKeywords: AM sidebands fc plus minus fm

learningObjectives: Calculate the AM modulation index mu = Am/Ac and predict the envelope limits Ac +/- Am
Predict the frequencies and heights of the AM spectral lines (fc with height Ac, and fc +/- fm with height Am/2) and the AM bandwidth 2fm
Calculate the FM peak deviation delta f = kf Am, the modulation index beta = delta f / fm and Carson's bandwidth 2(delta f + fm)
Compare AM and FM in the time domain and the frequency domain: which property of the carrier carries the message, and how the bandwidth depends on Am and fm
Explain over-modulation (mu > 1) in AM and the vanishing FM carrier line at beta of about 2.405
prerequisites: Amplitude, frequency and phase of a sinusoid

misconceptions.misconception: A louder message widens an AM signal
misconceptions.correction: AM sidebands always sit at fc +/- fm, so the AM bandwidth is 2fm whatever Am is; in FM the bandwidth does grow with Am
misconceptions.evidence: Raise Am from 50 to 150 at fm = 2 Hz: the AM lines stay at 18 and 22 Hz (B = 4.0 Hz), while Carson's FM bandwidth grows from 9.0 to 19.0 Hz

misconceptions.misconception: The carrier is always the strongest spectral line
misconceptions.correction: The FM carrier line is Ac |J0(beta)|, which is zero near beta = 2.405 even though the waveform keeps its full amplitude
misconceptions.evidence: FM with fc = 20 Hz, fm = 2 Hz: at Am = 96 (beta = 2.40) the carrier line falls to about 0.3 while the time plot still peaks at 100

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Analog modulation over a 1 second window. Radio buttons choose AM, FM, or both. Four sliders set the carrier amplitude, message amplitude, carrier frequency and message frequency. The plots show the modulated signal with its envelope or message and, in AM or FM mode, its amplitude spectrum with the bandwidth marked.

colorScheme.accent: red for AM, blue for FM, gold for bandwidth

controls.label: Modulation
controls.description: Shows AM (signal and spectrum), FM (signal and spectrum), or the AM and FM signals stacked on the same scale

controls.label: Carrier amplitude Ac
controls.description: Amplitude of the carrier in arbitrary units; sets the AM carrier line and the constant FM amplitude

controls.label: Message amplitude Am
controls.description: Amplitude of the message; sets the AM index mu = Am/Ac and the FM peak deviation 0.05 Am Hz

controls.label: Carrier frequency fc (Hz)
controls.description: Frequency of the carrier; with the 1 s window it equals the number of carrier cycles shown

controls.label: Message frequency fm (Hz)
controls.description: Frequency of the message; sets the spacing of the sideband lines

visualElements.description: AM signal (red) with its dashed envelope +/-(Ac + m(t)) and an over-modulation note
FM signal (blue) with the dashed message m(t)
One-sided amplitude spectrum with labeled carrier and sideband lines and a gold bar marking the bandwidth (2fm for AM, Carson's rule for FM)
Read-outs of the equation, mu, sideband power, delta f, beta, instantaneous-frequency range and bandwidth

model.description: Tone-modulated AM and FM over a 1 s window; the spectrum is a 4096-point FFT of a 10 s record (0.1 Hz bins)
equations: m(t) = Am sin(2 pi fm t)
AM: s(t) = [Ac + m(t)] sin(2 pi fc t), mu = Am / Ac
FM: s(t) = Ac sin(2 pi fc t - beta cos(2 pi fm t)), beta = kf Am / fm, kf = 0.05 Hz per unit

instructionalStrategies: Predict the line frequencies and heights, then verify them on the spectrum
Compare AM and FM for the same message in the AM + FM view
Search for the FM carrier null
extensions: Add an envelope detector to show the distortion caused by over-modulation
Replace the tone message with a two-tone message to show intermodulation-free AM sidebands
